class.name: PolyMeshND
class.brief_description: Base class for ND polyhedral meshes.
class.description: PolyMeshND is the base class for all ND polyhedral meshes. Polyhedral meshes are defined using a hierarchy of geometric data, each level used by the next level. Each edge is made of 2 vertices, each face is made of edges, each cell is made of faces, and so on for as many dimensions as the mesh has, mimicking the structure of OFF files, except for faces referencing edges instead of vertices directly. For a mesh of N dimensions, the (N-1)-dimensional cells are the boundary or surface of the mesh, and the optional N-dimensional cells encode hypervolumes made of boundary cells. Polyhedral meshes inherit [CellMeshND], and can be used anywhere a CellMeshND is expected. However, they are much slower than other types of cell meshes, such as [ArrayCellMeshND]. Polyhedral meshes are useful when high-level editing of the mesh is needed, for the same reasons that N-gon meshes are useful in 3D modeling applications such as Blender. The simplex cell indices, normals, and texture mapping are generated on demand, regardless of which getter is called first. If there are no boundary cells, or all boundary cells are shared by multiple hypervolumes, these arrays are empty. To make a PolyMeshND, use one of the descendant classes, such as [ArrayPolyMeshND] or [BoxPolyMeshND]. Advanced users can create custom polyhedral mesh classes by extending PolyMeshND.

method.name: _get_poly_cell_boundary_normals
method.description: Callback method that should return the boundary normals of the (N-1)-dimensional boundary cells, one per cell. Do not call this method. This can be overridden by derived classes when creating a custom mesh type in GDScript or another scripting language. See [method get_poly_cell_boundary_normals] for details of the returned data.

method.name: _get_poly_cell_boundary_pivot_overrides
method.description: Callback method that should return the pivot override indices of the (N-1)-dimensional boundary cells, one per cell. Do not call this method. This can be overridden by derived classes when creating a custom mesh type in GDScript or another scripting language. See [method get_poly_cell_boundary_pivot_overrides] for details of the returned data.

method.name: _get_poly_cell_indices
method.description: Callback method that should return the cell indices of a polyhedral mesh. Do not call this method. This can be overridden by derived classes when creating a custom mesh type in GDScript or another scripting language. See [method get_poly_cell_indices] for details of the returned data.

method.name: _get_poly_cell_texture_map
method.description: Callback method that should return the texture mapping of the polyhedral cells. Do not call this method. This can be overridden by derived classes when creating a custom mesh type in GDScript or another scripting language. See [method get_poly_cell_texture_map] for details of the returned data.

method.name: _get_poly_cell_vertex_normals
method.description: Callback method that should return the vertex normals of the polyhedral cells. Do not call this method. This can be overridden by derived classes when creating a custom mesh type in GDScript or another scripting language. See [method get_poly_cell_vertex_normals] for details of the returned data.

method.name: _get_poly_cell_vertex_positions
method.description: Callback method that should return the vertex positions of the polyhedral cells. Do not call this method. This can be overridden by derived classes when creating a custom mesh type in GDScript or another scripting language. See [method get_poly_cell_vertex_positions] for details of the returned data.

method.name: get_all_cell_vertex_indices
method.description: Returns the vertex indices of each (N-1)-dimensional boundary cell in the form of an array of [PackedInt32Array]s, by drilling down through the polyhedral hierarchy. If [param start_with_canonical_span] is [code]true[/code], the first N vertices of each cell form the canonical span used to determine the cell's orientation, where swapping the order of a cell's first two members flips its normal vector. [b]Note:[/b] This is not a trivial operation, consider caching the result if you need the same data multiple times.

method.name: get_all_face_vertex_indices
method.description: Returns the vertex indices of each face in the form of an array of [PackedInt32Array]s, by drilling down through the polyhedral hierarchy. [b]Note:[/b] This is not a trivial operation, consider caching the result if you need the same data multiple times.

method.name: get_all_poly_cell_poly_indices
method.description: Returns the indices of the cells at the given [param decomposition_dimension] that make up each cell of the given [param cell_dimension]. Both parameters mean 0 for 0D vertices, 1 for 1D edges, 2 for 2D faces, 3 for 3D cells, and so on for higher dimensions. The [param decomposition_dimension] MUST NOT be greater than the [param cell_dimension], and equality is a degenerate case where the "decomposition" of a cell into its own dimension is just itself.

method.name: get_all_poly_cell_vertex_indices
method.description: Returns the vertex indices of each cell of a given dimension in the form of an array of [PackedInt32Array]s, by drilling down through the polyhedral hierarchy. The [param cell_dimension] parameter specifies which polyhedral cell dimension to return, where 2 means 2D faces, 3 means 3D cells, and so on for higher dimensions. If [param start_with_canonical_span] is [code]true[/code], the first vertices of each cell form the canonical span used to determine the cell's orientation. [b]Note:[/b] This is not a trivial operation, consider caching the result if you need the same data multiple times.

method.name: get_poly_cell_boundary_normals
method.description: Returns the boundary normals of the (N-1)-dimensional boundary cells, one per cell.

method.name: get_poly_cell_boundary_pivot_overrides
method.description: The overrides for the pivot vertex of each boundary cell, providing control over how the cell is decomposed into simplexes for rendering. Each integer in this array is an index into the poly cell vertices array, specifying which vertex should be used as the pivot point for the corresponding cell when decomposing it into simplexes, or [code]-1[/code] to not override the pivot of that cell. The pivot for each boundary cell does not have to be one of the vertices on the sides, it can also be in the middle of the cell. This SHOULD be a vertex that can "see" all parts of the cell, meaning it only works for poly cells that are star-shaped.

method.name: get_poly_cell_indices
method.description: Returns the hierarchical polyhedral cell indices in the form of an array of arrays of [PackedInt32Array]s. This is the foundational data structure of [PolyMeshND]. Each item of the top level array holds the cells of one dimension, starting with 2D faces: - The first item is an array of 2D faces. It is an array of [PackedInt32Array]s, where each [PackedInt32Array] contains the 1D edge indices that make up one 2D face. - The second item is an array of 3D cells. It is an array of [PackedInt32Array]s, where each [PackedInt32Array] contains the 2D face indices that make up one 3D cell. - Each following item is an array of cells of the next dimension up, where each [PackedInt32Array] contains the indices of the cells of the previous dimension that make up one cell. For a mesh of N dimensions, the (N-1)-dimensional cells are the boundary of the mesh, and the optional last item holds N-dimensional hypervolume cells made of boundary cell indices. Since edges are always made of exactly 2 vertices, they are not included in this array. Edges use a simpler data structure where all edges are stored in a single [PackedInt32Array], and every 2 items represent one edge. See [method MeshND.get_edge_indices].

method.name: get_poly_cell_texture_map
method.description: Returns the texture mapping of the polyhedral boundary cells. Each item in this array is an array of [PackedFloat64Array]s containing the texture space mapping for the vertex instances of the corresponding boundary cell. Each [PackedFloat64Array] in these arrays defines the (N-1)-dimensional texture coordinates for the corresponding vertex instance in the cell, and is usually on the range from 0.0 to 1.0 on each axis. For example, a 4D mesh has 3D texture coordinates. The outer array may be empty for no texture mapping. Otherwise, it must contain one array per boundary cell; an individual cell's array may be empty for no texture mapping on that cell.

method.name: get_poly_cell_vertex_normals
method.description: Returns the normals of the vertex instances for each polyhedral boundary cell. Each item in this array is an array of [PackedFloat64Array]s containing the normals for each vertex instance in the corresponding boundary cell. Each [PackedFloat64Array] in these arrays is an N-dimensional vector that should be normalized.

method.name: get_poly_cell_vertex_positions
method.description: Returns the vertex positions of the polyhedral mesh. Each [PackedFloat64Array] in the array is a position in meters in ND space. The items in this array are referenced by the [method MeshND.get_edge_indices] array. [b]Note:[/b] The vertices returned by [method MeshND.get_vertex_positions] may be longer than this array. This is because [method MeshND.get_vertex_positions] returns the vertices used for decomposing the polyhedral mesh into simplexes, which may include extra virtual vertices added to keep the simplexes of adjacent cells aligned with each other. Regardless, the start of the array returned by [method MeshND.get_vertex_positions] will always match this array, such that it is either a superset of this array, or identical to it.

method.name: get_source_poly_cell_for_simplex_cell
method.description: Returns the index of the polyhedral boundary cell from which the given simplex cell was derived. This is useful for mapping simplex cells back to their original polyhedral boundary cells, for example when performing raycasts against the decomposed mesh and wanting to know which polyhedral cell was hit. Returns [code]-1[/code] if the given index is out of range of the cached simplex cells.

method.name: poly_mesh_clear_cache
method.description: Clears any cached data used by the polyhedral mesh, such as a cached simplex decomposition and its corresponding simplex normals and simplex texture map.

method.name: to_array_poly_mesh
method.description: Converts this polyhedral mesh into an [ArrayPolyMeshND], copying all mesh data into the new mesh. This is useful for converting specific polyhedral mesh types into a standard array-based representation for easier processing and manipulation. This performs a deep copy of all mesh data, except for the material, which is shared by default.
